Our mission ends when the financial barriers to obtaining and owning a high-quality service dog are eliminated and the public's knowledge of the disability community and its rights is second nature.

At Illini Service Dogs, our mission is to provide world-class service dogs to individuals who have a physical disability. We believe that through community education, advocating for disability rights and providing service dogs 100% free of charge, we are making the world a better place, four paws at a time.

We do this by giving University of Illinois students the unprecedented opportunity to train service dogs and engage with the disability community. Student members work one-on-one with our service dogs in training and experienced training staff to build the exact skill set the receiving individual needs. Along the way, each student gains a unique perspective on disability culture and rights.

It costs about $10,000 to $15,000 to train one service dog. Every dollar comes from donors like you, and every dog is placed free of charge.

It all started with a girl, a dog, and a dream. Illini Service Dogs was founded in 2010 at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. As a student, Bridget Evans proposed having college students foster and train service dogs for people with physical disabilities, and with a group of passionate, dedicated volunteers she began the first program in the country to let college students train mobility service dogs.

Bridget was born with spina bifida and got her first puppy, a big black Lab named Coal, when she was 11. She had been on several service dog waiting lists for years, most of which required a significant donation. So Bridget and her family began training Coal themselves, and a successful team was created. Coal went to high school with Bridget and gave her independence, purpose and passion. By the time she went to college, she had helped train over 20 service dogs. Coal passed away in 2013, but his legacy lives on in this organization and every service dog team he helped create.

Today ISD is a completely volunteer-run 501(c)(3) organization, formed by Bridget and people with backgrounds in animal rescue, animal behavior and non-profit work. Together we educate, fundraise and advocate for people with disabilities and service dogs, and strive to create a generation of partners in disability rights.

Illini Service Dogs is led by three boards. The Administrative Board oversees the organization as a whole and votes on key decisions; one of its seven members is the executive liaison, who is also president of the Executive Board. The Advisory Board brings specialized skills and acts as a sub-committee that advises the Administrative Board. The Executive Board is made up of University of Illinois students, elected every spring, who run day-to-day operations on campus. Every board member volunteers their time outside of school and work.

Our success comes from two things: members who volunteer their time outside their academic and professional careers, and our generous sponsors. Whether through a monetary gift, the donation of a dog, or services and facilities, these people and organizations have made ISD what it is today.

Illini Service Dogs is 100% funded through donations, which means every little bit counts. Whether you can give $1 or $10,000, no amount is too small. Your gift goes toward necessities like dog food, veterinary care and training supplies, plus fun things like toys!

To sponsor one of our dogs, email us. A $10,000 gift sponsors a dog for its entire training period (about 2 years), and donors who give $5,000 or more receive naming rights for the next dog to enter our program (names must be approved by the board of directors).

We specialize in training mobility service dogs for people with physical disabilities, and can accommodate certain specialized needs on a case-by-case basis. At this time we do not train psychiatric support dogs for mental health disabilities such as PTSD or anxiety. Our dogs are placed 100% free of charge.

Illini Service Dogs does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, age or sex. If you're unsure whether we can help you, email us. Your privacy is important to us: all applicant information is kept confidential.

Illini Service Dogs does not operate on a first come, first served basis. Each year we evaluate our list of applicants and determine whose needs best match the skills of our dogs nearing the end of their training. Due to a recent increase in demand, we no longer quote estimated wait times, and we encourage all applicants to seek out other ways of acquiring a service dog while waiting to hear from us.
Apply: Complete ISD's online service dog application.
Review: Once your application is reviewed, a representative contacts you about whether it was approved.
Waitlist: Approved applicants are placed on our waiting list.
Matching: Each year we match applicants' needs with the skills of dogs nearing the end of training.
Placement: If a match is found, we reach out to begin the placement process.

Puppy raisers are volunteers who foster a service dog in training until the dog is ready to move to the University of Illinois campus. Living with a puppy raiser gives our dogs lots of one-on-one socialization and training time to practice basic commands and good behavior.

The dog can be anywhere from 8 weeks to 2.5 years old. The length of each placement is decided together with the puppy raiser, but usually runs 2 to 6 months. Currently, puppy raisers must live in the Champaign-Urbana area.

Our dogs wear their vest when they're working. A working dog needs to stay focused on its handler, so please don't pet, call or feed it. Talk to the person, not the dog.

When the vest comes off, our dogs know it's time to play. That's the right moment to ask whether you can say hi.
